title: Baltasar Gracián (1601–1658) — Secret Museums, Baroque Warfare, and the Three Hundred Razors of Prudence

teenKit.tldr: In 1658, a brilliant Spanish Jesuit priest named Baltasar Gracián was publicly humiliated on a freezing stone floor because he secretly wrote the ultimate, cutthroat playbook for human survival and psychological power.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding Gracián's razor-sharp mind teaches you how power, reputation, and information actually flow through human institutions, giving you a survival manual for navigating politics and social structures today.
keyTakeaways: Baltasar Gracián lived a double life as both a devoted religious priest and the mastermind behind some of history's coldest psychological maxims.
His masterworks, like El Criticón and the Oráculo manual, functioned as secret museums of human behavior, dissecting how people manipulate perception and social standing.
Gracián ultimately violated his own golden rule of prudence—Maxim 7, which warns against self-exposure—by risking everything to keep his explosive literary masterpieces alive.
